deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous page): this is §2, 'global stratifications: simplicial formalism (without tubes)'. X is a topological space (later to become an arbitrary topos). I is an ordered set and (X_i)_{i∈I} is a family of subspaces of X such that (a) the X_i are closed and the family is locally finite, and (b) i ≤ j implies X_i ⊂ X_j. The X_i should be thought of as the closures of the strata. X_{Δ0} = ⊔_i X_i = {(x,i) ∈ X×I | x ∈ X_i}.

This page:
(3) There is a canonical map ε: X_{Δ0} → X. Hypothesis (a) says ε is separated and finite, i.e. proper with finite fibres. On each summand it is a closed embedding, so ε is also a local immersion.
(4)-(5) Define the closed subspace X_{Δ1} ⊂ X_{Δ0}×X_{Δ0} = ⊔_{(i,j)} X_i×X_j as ⊔_{i≤j} Γ_{ij}. Here Γ_{ij} ⊂ X_i×X_j is the graph of the inclusion X_i ↪ X_j. So X_{Δ1} ≅ ⊔_{i≤j} X_i, a copy of X_i for each arrow i ≤ j.
(6)-(7) There are two projections a, b: X_{Δ1} → X_{Δ0} (source and target).
- a (source, written σ in (7)) sends the copy Γ_{ij} identically onto X_i. Over X_i it is the constant covering X_i × I_i with I_i = {j ≥ i}. Hence a is an étale covering, and a finite one when the I_i are finite.
- b (target) sends the copy Γ_{ij} onto X_j via the closed embedding X_i ↪ X_j. Hence b is a local immersion.

The next page identifies X_{Δ1} as the graph of the order relation (x,i) ≤ (y,j) ⇔ x = y and i ≤ j. This makes (X_{Δ0}, X_{Δ1}) an internal poset, hence an internal category, in Top. Composition comes from X_{Δ2} = X_{Δ1} ×_{X_{Δ0}} X_{Δ1}. Its nerve is the simplicial space X_{Δn} = ⊔_{i0≤…≤in} X_{i0}, augmented to X.

Purpose: to encode a global stratification by a simplicial (internal-category) object whose face maps are étale coverings or local immersions. This is a combinatorial skeleton, before 'tubes' are introduced, to be later sheafified on X and generalised to a topos as base.
errors: Grothendieck writes 'donc rev. fini si les I_i sont finis', but the hypotheses already force this. If X_i ≠ ∅ and x ∈ X_i, then x ∈ X_j for every j ≥ i, so local finiteness of the family (X_j) forces I_i to be finite. The proviso is therefore automatic for nonempty X_i.

That X_{Δ1} (each Γ_{ij}) is closed in X_{Δ0}×X_{Δ0} needs X to be separated (closed diagonal). For a general topological space the graph of an inclusion need not be closed. The previous page imposes no Hausdorff hypothesis, which is a small gap.

ideas.what: Disjoint union of the closed strata-closures, mapping finitely (proper, finite fibres) and as a local immersion onto X
ideas.modern_name: Normalization-type resolution of a closed cover / the 0-simplices of a semi-simplicial resolution
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (cf. Deligne's simplicial resolutions in Hodge III; descent along closed covers in SGA 4)
ideas.where_published: Closed-cover descent appears in SGA 4 (Vbis/proper descent context); not in this precise form

ideas.what: Internal poset/category in Top with objects ⊔X_i and arrows ⊔_{i≤j}Γ_{ij}; source map an étale covering, target map a local immersion
ideas.modern_name: Internal category (topological category) attached to a poset-filtered space; nerve as a simplicial space; related to Grothendieck construction of the functor I → Top, i ↦ X_i
ideas.usually_credited_to: General internal-category formalism (Ehresmann, Grothendieck); for stratified spaces, cf. later exit-path/décollage approaches (MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie HA App. A, Haine, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka)
ideas.where_published: Only allusions to 'dévissage des structures stratifiées' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

missed.claim: A partial step in Grothendieck's unpublished project on 'stratified topoi': he encodes a global stratification as an internal poset in Top (later in a topos), whose source map is a constant étale covering and whose target map is a local immersion. He does this before introducing tubes, deliberately separating the combinatorial (simplicial) part from the tubular data. Mathematically the page is elementary, but it documents his chosen axiomatics (étale/local-immersion face maps), which differs in emphasis from later exit-path-category approaches.
missed.quote: X_{Δ1} →a X_{Δ0} est un revêtement étale (en fait constant sur chaque X_i ...) b) X_{Δ1} →b X_{Δ0} est une immersion locale.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of historical interest for comparison with modern stratified homotopy theory (décollages, conically stratified ∞-topoi). Mathematically the content is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine set-up: the nerve of the internal poset formed by the closed strata, with elementary properties of its face maps. It is interesting only as documentation of the unpublished 'topos stratifié' programme.
transcription_corrections: In (7a) the arrow label above X_{Δ1} → X_{Δ0} appears to be 'σ' (or a stylised 'a'), consistent with 'a' in (6); the source map.
'séparé' is a marginal insertion before 'et à fibres finies', and 'fini' is underlined. The reading is 'est fini — i.e. propre et à fibres finies', with 'séparé' added in the margin.
In (4) the notation under the equals sign reads 'déf' (by definition).
